methodology.note: Source review locked before any HorusTrace scan of this cohort. Findings are conservative and distinguish model-driven authority from deterministic/application-only flows.

findings.title: Bound stdio MCP catalogue executes without a source-visible per-call approval boundary
evidence: search/agent.py:root LlmAgent binds search_youtube as a model-callable tool
findings.rationale: The agent can invoke a tool catalogue supplied by the external mcp-youtube-search package. The concrete catalogue/sinks are outside the repository, so they must remain unresolved rather than invented; however the MCP authority is source-bound and no per-call approval or allowlist boundary is visible.

limitations: Concrete MCP tools and their downstream sinks are not present in the repository.

findings.title: Task-controlled RiskGuard URL reaches a server-side A2A/HTTP destination
findings.rationale: An externally supplied task payload can select the RiskGuard service URL that the deterministic AlphaBot workflow dereferences. This is dynamic server-side destination authority, but it is not model-selected LLM authority and should be qualified accordingly.

cases.precision_control: The repository proposes and risk-checks trades but source does not show a broker/exchange execution sink; do not report actual trade execution authority.

findings.title: Model-callable grocery tool performs persistent MongoDB cart writes without explicit approval
findings.rationale: User requests can cause the ADK agent to invoke add_to_cart, which persistently mutates the carts collection. The prompt tells the model to search first, but no code-level human approval/guardrail is visible around the write.

cases.precision_control: The public WebSocket can invoke deep_research, but the model-callable research authority is read-only/fixed-provider Tavily search in source. Do not upgrade this to arbitrary egress or state-changing authority solely because ingress is public.

findings.title: Model-selected Box object identifiers can read and AI-process broadly accessible Box content
evidence: box_agent/sub_agents/box_agent.py binds box_read_tool, folder listing, Box AI ask/extract tools
findings.rationale: The LLM can select Box file/folder identifiers and retrieve or AI-process content available to the CCG client. No source-visible resource allowlist or user-specific object authorization boundary is applied by these wrappers.

cases.precision_control: The bound Pydantic tool performs read-only retrieval from the configured knowledge base. Source does not show file/process execution, persistent mutation, or model-selected arbitrary network destinations; do not infer them.

Retrieved source content is withheld from synthesis until approved_chunk_ids contains explicit user selections. The search tool returns summaries/state, and synthesize_with_sources refuses to expose source content when no chunks are approved. Preserve this approval boundary.

findings.title: Slack mention input can trigger a model-selected external reaction write without explicit approval
evidence: pydantic-ai/listeners/events/app_mentioned.py passes cleaned Slack mention text into run_agent
findings.rationale: Untrusted Slack mention content reaches the Pydantic agent, whose built-in tool can write a reaction to Slack. No per-call human approval is visible.

findings.title: User-token-authenticated Slack MCP authority is dynamically attached without source-visible per-call approval
evidence: pydantic-ai/agent/agent.py:run_agent conditionally constructs MCPToolset('https://mcp.slack.com/mcp', Authorization: Bearer deps.user_token)
SYSTEM_PROMPT explicitly describes Slack MCP search/read/send/schedule/create/update capabilities
findings.rationale: When a user token is present, the runtime binds a remote Slack MCP catalogue to the agent. The endpoint is fixed and user-scoped, but the source-visible authority includes read and write actions and shows no per-call approval/allowlist boundary. Concrete remote tool definitions remain external.

limitations: Remote Slack MCP tool definitions are not stored in the repository; do not invent individual MCP tool sinks beyond the source-declared capability set.

findings.title: Interactive CLI input reaches shell execution with execution approval explicitly disabled
findings.rationale: The default CLI example exposes command execution to the model and explicitly disables execute approval. The local backend is enabled for execution unless --no-execute is supplied.

findings.title: Interactive CLI input reaches filesystem mutation with write approval disabled and optional confinement
evidence: examples/local_cli/cli_agent.py:allowed_directories=[working_dir] only when --restrict is set; default is None
SYSTEM_PROMPT directs the agent to create/edit files
findings.rationale: The model has source-visible file-write/edit authority with approval disabled. Working-directory confinement is opt-in rather than the default.

cases.precision_control: The same repository also contains READONLY_RULESET examples where write/edit/execute tools are hidden; scanner findings must remain instance/configuration specific rather than collapsing all agents into the permissive example.

The repository provides reusable dynamic-subagent/delegation infrastructure, including capability factories and model allowlists, but the Python source does not establish a concrete application/root agent with privileged capabilities. Do not convert library capability into deployed agent authority.
